text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Jordanian soldier Ahmed Daqamsa sentenced to life imprisonment with hard labour for shooting Israeli girls. Israel satisfied with the ruling.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali to meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Ramallah today.
- U.S. Senate agrees to increase annual aid to Jordan to $150 million. Egypt still gets $2.1 billion and Israel $3 billion.
- Professional unions call for boycott of parliamentary elections.
- Government to announce measures shortly to give locally manufactured goods preference over foreign goods in government tenders.

- Moslem Brotherhood's boycott call has snowballed. Islamic Action Front, the Brotherhood's political arm, call for a meeting of their consultative council on Thursday which is expected to support the boycott. But the front's secretary-general says participation is better than boycotting.
- Jordan's mad cow committee recommends lifting ban on imports of cow's milk and milk products from Britain, Switzerland, Portugal, France and Holland.
- Sources say minister of finance will announce within days a list of 40 primary products used in Jordanian industry which will be exempted from customs or have their duties cut.
- Arafat, King Hussein and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak expected to meet by the end of the month, PLO official Asad Abdul-Rahman says.
- Visit of Syrian Industry Minister Ahmad Nezamuldin is a sign that there might soon be a meeting of the joint higher council. Jordanian-Syrian relations get back to the economic basics.
- Government approves a one-month marketing month for Jordan next year to coincide with the cultural festival of Jerash.
- Islamic Action Front executive council endorses poll boycott. Party's Shura council will convene for final decision next Thursday.
